claim: The Lancet Global Health Commission identifies medical oxygen security as a cross-cutting health-system requirement and estimates that roughly 374 million newborns, children, and adults need medical oxygen each year, with 82 percent of these patients in low- and middle-income countries.

source.title: The Lancet Global Health Commission on medical oxygen security

method: Reviewed commission abstract and policy framing for oxygen-system scope, health-service areas, and LMIC access-failure framing.
limitations: Commission framing supports pack selection but does not by itself prove country-level oxygen readiness.
Global synthesis cannot replace facility-level functionality, uptime, power, consumables, or clinical-use measurement.

claim: World Health Assembly resolution WHA76.3 asks Member States to strengthen medical oxygen systems, including planning, procurement, distribution, maintenance, regulation, training, and monitoring.

source.title: Increasing access to medical oxygen: resolution WHA76.3

method: Reviewed the adopted World Health Assembly resolution for requested Member State actions and system components named in the resolution text.
limitations: Resolution proves institutional recognition and action categories, not implementation progress.
It does not quantify country-level gaps or rank investment options.

claim: WHO's technical specifications describe multiple oxygen source and distribution options, making equipment choice dependent on demand, facility level, power, maintenance, and supply-chain context.

source.title: Oxygen sources and distribution for COVID-19 treatment centres: interim guidance

method: Reviewed WHO guidance for oxygen source categories, distribution options, and operational constraints relevant to readiness classification.
limitations: COVID-era guidance is not a complete oxygen-system assessment method.
The document supports technical classification but not current facility readiness.

claim: The WHO-UNICEF Global Report on Assistive Technology estimates that more than 2.5 billion people need at least one assistive product, but this comparator problem is broader and generally less time-critical than acute oxygen access failure.
method: Reviewed WHO publication page and report framing for global need estimates used in discovery-mode candidate comparison.
limitations: Comparator evidence only; it does not support oxygen-specific claims.
Need for assistive products is not equivalent to untreated acute mortality risk.

claim: WHO estimates that rabies causes about 59,000 human deaths annually, mostly in Asia and Africa, making it a severe but narrower comparator problem for discovery-mode ranking.
method: Reviewed WHO rabies fact sheet for global death estimate, geographic concentration, and prevention pathway used as discovery-mode comparator evidence.
limitations: Comparator evidence only; it does not support oxygen-specific claims.
Fact sheet does not quantify the current funding or surveillance gap for each country.
